question: The Federal Structure, Judiciary, Governor System and Emergency Powers — these features of the Indian Constitution are drawn from the:________
solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act of 1935**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act of 1935 was a major legislative act passed by the British Parliament that laid the foundation for the establishment of federal structure in India.
 
• This Act introduced provincial autonomy and proposed a federal structure of government, which later influenced the Indian Constitution significantly.
 
• The Act also established the Federal Court of India, which was the precursor to the Supreme Court of India.
 
• Emergency powers were also detailed in this act, allowing the British authorities to suspend the autonomy of the provinces in times of emergency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Federal Structure:**

 
 
• The Government of India Act of 1935 provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation consisting of provinces and princely states as units.
 
• This federal structure laid down the division of powers between the central government and the provinces.
 
 
 
• **Judiciary:**
 
 
• The Act established the Federal Court of India, which was the highest court in India until the establishment of the Supreme Court in 1950.
 
• The Federal Court had original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions.
 
 
 
• **Governor System:**
 
 
• The Act provided for the office of the Governor in each province, who was appointed by the British Crown.
 
• The Governor had substantial powers, including the power to override the decisions of the elected provincial governments.
 
 
 
• **Emergency Powers:**
 
 
• The Government of India Act of 1935 empowered the Governor-General to assume greater control over the provinces in case of a breakdown of constitutional machinery or during emergencies.
 
• These powers were a precursor to the emergency provisions laid down in the Indian Constitution.
